answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network binds each entity to a cryptographic stake burning mechanism where minting an identity burns a reserve token. An attacker attempting to scale counterfeit identities faces superlinear cost scaling via a quadratic penalty curve: deploying $n$ nodes costs $O(n^2)$ burnt capital. Like a petrified relic anchoring an underwater reef, permanent slashing burns scarce jade reserves on-chain, imposing catastrophic friction on duplicate agents.
